title: The Perseverance of the Saints
speaker: Elder Nick Anderson

outline.title: Statement of the Doctrine
subpoints: Those who are truly saved cannot fall away from the state of grace.
God begins a good work in believers and will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
The idea of God rejecting a saved person due to sin is not found in Scripture.

outline.title: The Golden Chain of Redemption
subpoints: Romans 8:28-30 presents an unbreakable chain of salvation.
Foreknowledge, predestination, calling, justification, and glorification are certain.
This sequence guarantees that those called by God will be glorified.

outline.title: Christ’s Promise of Eternal Life
subpoints: Jesus promises that those given eternal life shall never perish.
No one, including the believer themselves, can snatch them out of the Father’s hand.
Eternal life is unconditional and secure by divine power.

outline.title: The Work of the Holy Spirit
subpoints: Those born of God do not continue in sin because God’s seed remains in them.
The wicked one cannot touch or destroy the believer’s faith.

outline.title: Grounds of Perseverance
subpoints: Perseverance depends on God’s immutable decree of election, not human free will.
It rests on the merit and intercession of Jesus Christ.
It is secured by the abiding of the Spirit and the nature of the covenant of grace.

summary:
This Sunday school lesson examines Chapter 17 of the Westminster Confession of Faith, focusing on the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints. The teaching emphasizes that true believers are eternally secure, not because of their own ability to remain faithful, but because of God’s unchanging nature and power. The session highlights that if salvation depended on human effort, it would be impossible to maintain, leading to anxiety and a works-based faith rather than confidence in God’s grace.

The sermon explores several key biblical passages that support this doctrine, including the 'Golden Chain' in Romans 8, which outlines the unbreakable sequence from foreknowledge to glorification. It also references Jesus’ promise in John 10 that no one can snatch His sheep from the Father’s hand, and the writings of 1 John, which describe the internal transformation of those born of God. These texts collectively affirm that God’s initiative in salvation is both effective and permanent.

Finally, the lesson details the theological grounds for perseverance as outlined in the Confession: the immutability of the decree of election, the efficacy of Christ’s merit and intercession, and the abiding presence of the Holy Spirit. By grounding security in God’s immutable love and covenant faithfulness, believers are freed from the fear of apostasy and encouraged to live in humble confidence and gratitude.
